title: Retrieval triggers and reuse
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for looking up existing nouns before generating new ones and reusing past solutions safely: trigger rules for when to look first, a cheapest-first ladder from what is at hand to new research, fingerprints loose on the task and strict on the environment, solutions stored only after they regenerate their result alone, matches tried under the check with rollback, unmet needs matched against new arrivals, and reuse judged by verified work per unit of cost.
boundaries: A retrieved item is a prior, never proof. Only the check decides a reuse.
Lookups read the team's own nouns; nothing outside the team's scope is written.
Stored solutions are code nouns. The library never runs them; workers run them under their own permissions.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; an authorized requester enqueues the proposals worth doing.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for looking up existing nouns before generating and reusing past solutions safely

value.lets_workers: Look up what already exists before generating anything new, and reuse earlier solutions without trusting them blindly: fire lookup triggers, climb a ladder from what is at hand to new research, treat a fingerprint match as permission to try under the check, store only solutions that regenerate their result alone, record unmet needs so later arrivals can meet them, and judge all of it by verified work per unit of cost.

flow.when: Before any new noun or solution is generated.
When a lookup finds a fingerprint match; deterministic.
After a run verifies, before anything is stored for reuse.
When a stored solution is proposed for review or for procedural use; a different worker or a person.
When a lookup finds nothing suitable.
When new nouns, releases or indexed sources arrive.
Over a window of runs; deterministic.

guardrails: A retrieved item is a prior, never proof; only the check decides a reuse.
Loose on the task, strict on the environment.
Nothing promotes itself, and no run is credited with reusing its own output.
Reuse is judged by verified tasks per unit of total cost, not by how relevant results looked.

nouns.title: How lookups, reuse, qualification and saved needs fit together
nouns.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.

lifecycle: look-up-first applies the triggers and searches cheapest first, recording where it looked and the rung that answered.
try-reuse materializes a matched solution in a copy, lets the check decide and rolls back on a miss.
When generation was needed and the run verified, qualify-solution stores a body only if it regenerates the result alone.
review-promotion, by a different worker or a person, moves a solution to reviewed or, with two verified instances, to procedural.
When nothing fit, record-saved-need keeps the unmet need; match-arrivals checks new arrivals against it.
measure-reuse counts verified work per unit of cost over a window, against a baseline.
rules: Find the binding constraint first. Better search in front of a failing step improves nothing.
A saved need improves the system while it is idle, because the world changes underneath it.
Failures are stored too, under the same fingerprint, so refuted work is skipped instead of rediscovered.
Prefer a resolver for a class of failure that abstains when it does not apply over a cached answer for one task.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.

value.order: Cheapest first: what is at hand, the team's nouns, qualified solutions and tombstones, this library, then outside catalogs.

nouns.title: From what is at hand to new research, cheapest first
nouns.category_reason: A deterministic escalation order with a derived threshold.

rungs.means: The packet and state already answer it.
An existing noun answers as is.
An existing noun answers with settings changed.
An existing noun changed in place answers it.
Nothing fits; new work is generated.
Generating needs knowledge nobody holds; propose research.
Every route was tried on this fingerprint class with no verified outcome; say so and spend the allowance elsewhere.

value.ladder_rule: Keep trying the cheaper rung while its success rate is at least its cost divided by the next rung's cost. Derive the threshold from measured costs; do not tune it by feel.
value.record: Every lookup records the rung that answered, so the rates behind the rule exist.

nouns.title: Fingerprints that are loose on the task and strict on the environment
nouns.category_reason: Deterministic fingerprint construction and backoff rules.

value.step_key: The procedure digest, the state slice digest and the observation digest of a step.

levels.keys: step kind, check, failure class and files touched
source, check family and failure class

value.selection: Use the most specific level with at least two verified outcomes, and record which level answered.
value.loose_and_strict: Match the task loosely, because a wrong match costs one check run and a rollback. Match the environment exactly: runner version, model tier, interpreter and installed packages.
statistics: Smooth small counts so one success in one try is not read as certainty.
Scope every rate to an environment fingerprint; when the environment changes, earlier rates describe another system.
A crashed or unrecorded run is not counted.

nouns.title: What a solution must survive before it is stored for reuse

steps: Distill a script or resolver that regenerates the result, as its own step; asking the solving step to also write one does not work reliably.
Delete the deliverables.
Replay the body alone in a clean copy.
The check must pass again, or the body is refused.
Recitation guard: refuse a body whose literals hold three or more numbers that appear in the deliverable but in no input.
Store the body by digest with its constraints, its check, its fingerprint and the lookup that came before it.

memory_bars.semantic: review by someone other than the producer

value.separation: Producer, reviewer and promoter are different. A run never promotes its own lesson and is never credited with reusing what it produced itself.
value.resolvers: A resolver abstains when it does not apply; one that guesses is refused.

nouns.title: How each retrieved fact is known
nouns.category_reason: A fixed vocabulary for the provenance of retrieved facts.

methods.parsed: A syntactic read says the thing exists, such as a call in source text.
methods.resolved: A compiler, index or registry resolved the reference.
methods.observed: Seen happening at run time; valid only for the environment it ran in, so carry that environment's digest.
methods.reported: Someone else said so; not reproduced here.
methods.designed: Intent only; nothing built or measured.

value.rule: A fact without a method is treated as reported. Cheap to add at the start, impossible to retrofit honestly.

nouns.title: Record checks for qualified solutions, with made-up golden solutions
nouns.category_reason: A deterministic check suite with known-good and known-bad examples; the validator recomputes every verdict.

value.purpose: Checks every stored solution must pass before any worker reuses it. The two made-up good solutions pass all of them; each made-up bad solution fails exactly the one check named in fails.

deterministic_checks.why: Qualification starts by deleting the deliverables, so the stored body must regenerate them.
The body is replayed by itself in a clean copy, not inside the run that produced it.
The check must pass again on the replay, or nothing is stored.
A body that pastes its answers instead of computing them is refused.
The environment side of the fingerprint is exact; a replay elsewhere is a different claim.
Every stored solution names the check that decides each reuse.
The search that came first is kept, so later runs can learn which lookups pay.
One success is an anecdote; a procedure needs two verified instances.
Nothing promotes itself: a reviewed or procedural solution was reviewed by someone other than its producer.

verbs.title: Look up existing nouns before generating
verbs.summary: Apply the trigger rules to a request, search cheapest first among what is at hand, the team's nouns, qualified solutions, tombstones and this library, and record the candidates, their fit and the rung that answered.
verbs.outcome: A lookup record with a decision to reuse, adapt, generate, research or abstain.

slots.name: request
slots.description: Pin of the request or task.

steps: Verify the pins. Fire the triggers before any generation; record which fired.
Search in the ladder's order and record every search, including those that found nothing.
Skip a candidate whose fingerprint has a refutation or tombstone, and say so.
Label each candidate's evidence by how it is known.
Propose try-reuse for a fitting match, record-saved-need when nothing fits, or the prior-art survey for something new and reusable.

acceptance.check: The lookup validates against template.lookup-record's schema.
searched lists at least one place, with its query and result count.
rung_answered is generated or later only when no candidate fit.

network: Read-only searches of the team's own nouns on its assigned fabric; nothing is written there.

verbs.title: Try a stored solution under the check
verbs.summary: Treat a fingerprint match as permission to try: confirm the environment fingerprint matches, materialize the stored solution in a copy, let the check decide, and roll back every touched file on a miss.
verbs.outcome: A reuse attempt: verified reuse, a rolled-back miss, or a refusal for environment drift or a tombstone.
steps: Verify the pins. Refuse before materializing when the environment fingerprint differs or a tombstone matches.
Materialize the body in a copy and run the named check yourself.
On a failed check, roll back every touched file, record the miss and propose generation.

acceptance.check: The attempt validates against template.reuse-attempt's schema.
outcome is verified_reuse only when check_exit is 0.
A miss lists every touched file in files_rolled_back.

network: Local copies and the local check command only.

verbs.title: Qualify a solution before storing it
verbs.summary: From a verified run, distill a body that regenerates the result, delete the deliverables, replay the body alone in a clean copy, require the check to pass again, apply the recitation guard and record its fingerprint and the lookup that came first.
verbs.outcome: A qualified solution with status candidate, or no_change when the replay fails.

slots.name: lookup
slots.description: Pin of the lookup that came first.

steps: Verify the pins and the run's verified grade.
Distill the body as its own step; then delete the deliverables and replay the body alone in a clean copy.
Refuse when the check fails on replay or the recitation guard trips; keep the refusal as a finding.
Store the body by digest with status candidate; promotion is a separate verb.

acceptance.check: The solution validates against template.qualified-solution's schema.
The solution passes every check in reuse-checks.
status is candidate when this verb writes it.

network: Local clean copies and the local check command only.

verbs.title: Review a stored solution for promotion
verbs.summary: A worker or person other than the producer rechecks a stored solution's qualification and verified instances and decides whether it becomes reviewed, procedural with two verified instances, stays a candidate, is rejected or is tombstoned.
verbs.outcome: A promotion decision with its evidence.
steps: Verify the pins. Confirm you are not the producer.
Recheck the qualification evidence and count verified instances; procedural needs at least two.
Tombstone a solution that verified wrongly, so lookups skip it.

acceptance.check: The decision validates against template.promotion-decision's schema.
promote_procedural only with verified_instances of at least 2.
The reviewer is not the solution's producer.

verbs.title: Record an unmet need
verbs.summary: When a lookup finds nothing suitable, record the need with its constraints, where it was searched, why nothing fit, a cheap filter and a fit rule, so later arrivals can be matched against it.
verbs.outcome: A saved need, or no_change when an open need already covers it.

slots.name: lookup
slots.description: Pin of the lookup that found nothing.

steps: Verify the pins. Reuse an open need of the same shape instead of adding a duplicate.
Write constraints a candidate must meet, and a cheap filter that shortlists without a model call.
Set an expiry; an expired need is withdrawn, not kept forever.

acceptance.check: The need validates against template.saved-need's schema.
Every searched place has a date.
The cheap filter uses terms and kinds only, with no model call.

verbs.title: Match new arrivals against open needs
verbs.summary: Check newly arrived nouns, releases, indexed sources and qualified solutions against every open saved need: shortlist with the cheap filter, check the constraints, judge fit only for what passes, and record which stage rejected each candidate.
verbs.outcome: An arrival match with recommendations, or no_change when nothing matched.

slots.name: needs
slots.description: Pins of the open saved needs.

steps: Verify the pins. Apply the cheap filter to every pair before anything else.
Check constraints next; spend a model call on fit only for pairs that passed both.
Record the stage that rejected each pair, and propose a reuse or trial for each recommendation.

acceptance.check: The match validates against template.arrival-match's schema.
Each stage's out count is at most its in count.
Each recommendation's evidence addresses every constraint of its need.

network: Read-only access to the team's own nouns and arrival records on its assigned fabric.

verbs.title: Measure whether reuse pays
verbs.summary: Over a window of recorded runs in one environment, count verified tasks against total cost with every model counted, hits and rollbacks by fingerprint level, self-reuse excluded, how often retrieved results had to be read directly anyway, and compare with a baseline window.
verbs.outcome: A reuse ledger with a verdict of reuse pays, no difference, reuse costs more or unknown.

slots.name: runs
slots.description: Pins of the recorded runs in the window.

baseline_window.description: The earlier window to compare with.

steps: Verify the pins. Count only runs recorded in the ledger's environment fingerprint.
Exclude any reuse of a run's own output, and count rollbacks as misses.
Compute verified tasks per thousand model calls for the window and the baseline; write unknown when either lacks counts.

acceptance.check: The ledger validates against template.reuse-ledger's schema.
verified_per_1000_calls recomputes from verified and model_calls for the window and the baseline.
rollbacks equals the sum of attempts minus verified across hits.
